items.reason: `lift` decodes into the grant used by dashboard snapshot ordering.
Only the shipped `active` preset enables Lift.
`pin` silently decodes into the same Lift field without alias findings.
The decoder gives `lift` precedence when both spellings appear.
Neither spelling leaves Lift false.
Both spellings receive nonfatal boolean validation through config findings.
dashboard/status_render.go still describes derived ordering as “nothing pins.”
Manual and unrelated pin terminology and behavior remain unchanged.
The field description, serialized key, and shipped grant use `lift`.
Sibling worktrees resolve to the same common directory and lift repository sets.
Checkout attribution retains its ranking and returns before the repository pass.
Task-set tag attribution returns before either locality pass.
Repository indexing includes both bound and unbound Task sets.
Repository lookup compares canonical git common directories.
Cursor keys still use project name and identifier, so collisions can lift another repository’s row.
Missing or unknown repository identities produce no attribution or status message.
The repository pass concatenates every answering kind, with a two-kind assertion.
Launch resolves repository identity once; a counting git seam checks five rebuilds.
Status supplies empty pane facts and never invokes repository attribution resolution.
Lifting operates only on admitted rows and preserves preset narrowing.
Arrived Maps remain visible under `active` and enter repository attribution, so non-live Maps also lift.
Repository answers merge Task sets before Maps, covered by a real-kind test.
Map session stamps retain precedence over repository attribution.
Routines implement neither locality seam, with comments and tests documenting the deliberate exclusion.

scores.rationale: Clear implementation with substantial tests, but repository collisions, Map lifecycle filtering, and an incomplete rename remain.
